### ElementComponentsOrError

ElementComponentsArrayItem or ErrorItem: The components of an element or an error.

### ElementComponentsOrErrorArray

array of ElementComponentsOrError: A list of element component lists or errors.

### ElementTrims

object: The trims of one element: the roofs and shells trimming it, and the elements it trims.
- `trimmedBy` (array of object, required): The roofs and shells trimming this element, with the trim type.
  - `elementId` (ElementId, required)
  - `trimType` (TrimType, required)
- `trims` (Elements, required): The elements this roof or shell trims.

### ElementTrimsOrError

ElementTrims or ErrorItem: The trims of one element, or an error.

### MergedElements

object: The elements merged with one element.
- `mergedElements` (Elements, required): The elements merged with the queried element. Empty when it is not merged with any.

### MergedElementsOrError

MergedElements or ErrorItem: The elements merged with one element, or an error.

### MEPRoutingSegmentDetails

object: The details of an MEP routing segment.
- `elementId` (ElementId, required)
- `routingElementId` (ElementId): The routing element the segment belongs to.
- `crossSectionWidth` (number, required)
- `crossSectionHeight` (number, required)
- `crossSectionShape` (string, required)
- `crossSectionReferenceId` (integer): The cross section reference id of the segment in its preference table (meaningful for circular cross sections).
- `preferenceTableId` (Guid): The guid of the segment preference table used by the segment (see GetMEPPreferenceTables).
- `beginNodeId` (ElementId): The routing node at the beginning of the segment.
- `endNodeId` (ElementId): The routing node at the end of the segment.
- `anchor` (MEPRoutingAnchor)
- `referenceLineOffsetX` (number): The horizontal offset of the reference line from the anchor point.
- `referenceLineOffsetY` (number): The vertical offset of the reference line from the anchor point.
- `wallThickness` (number): The wall thickness of the segment.
- `flangeSize` (number): The flange size of the segment (width for Ventilation, diameter for Piping). It is used only when the connection style is Flanged; Archicad 29 also returns it for other styles.
- `insulationThickness` (number): The insulation thickness of the rigid segments of the segment. Only present when they are insulated (never for cable carriers).
- `connectionStyle` (MEPConnectionStyle)
- `rigidSegments` (Elements): The rigid segments (the straight duct, pipe or cable carrier pieces) of the routing segment.

### MEPRoutingNodeDetails

object: The details of an MEP routing node.
- `elementId` (ElementId, required)
- `routingElementId` (ElementId): The routing element the node belongs to.
- `position` (Coordinate3D, required)
- `incomingSegmentId` (ElementId): The routing segment ending at this node. Not present at the beginning of the route.
- `outgoingSegmentId` (ElementId): The routing segment starting at this node. Not present at the end of the route.
- `preferredTransitionPlacement` (MEPPreferredTransitionPlacement)
- `elbows` (Elements): The elbows (bends in Archicad 28) at this node.
- `transitions` (Elements): The transitions at this node.

### MEPRoutingElementDetails

object: The details of an MEP routing element.
- `domain` (MEPDomainOrUnknown, required)
- `mepSystemId` (AttributeId, required)
- `floorIndex` (integer): The index of the home story of the routing element (see GetStories).
- `offsetFromHomeStory` (number): The offset of the lowest node of the routing element from the level of its home story.
- `branchPreferenceTableId` (Guid): The guid of the branch preference table used by the routing element (see GetMEPPreferenceTables). Not present when the routing element has none.
- `logicallyConnectedPortIdAtRouteBegin` (Guid): The port logically connected to the beginning of the route (see GetMEPPorts). Not present when nothing is connected there.
- `logicallyConnectedPortIdAtRouteEnd` (Guid): The port logically connected to the end of the route (see GetMEPPorts). Not present when nothing is connected there.
- `cutPlanePosition` (MEPCutPlanePosition)
- `floorPlanDisplayOption` (MEPFloorPlanDisplayOption)
- `showProjection` (MEPShowProjection)
- `onStoryVisibility` (MEPOnStoryVisibility)
- `polyline` (array of Coordinate3D, required)
- `segments` (array of MEPRoutingSegmentDetails, required)
- `nodes` (array of MEPRoutingNodeDetails, required)

### MEPRoutingElementDetailsOrError

MEPRoutingElementDetails or ErrorItem: The details of an MEP routing element or an error.

### MEPRoutingElementDetailsOrErrors

array of MEPRoutingElementDetailsOrError: A list of MEP routing element details or errors.

### MEPPortDetails

object: The details of a port of an MEP element.
- `portId` (Guid, required)
- `mepElementId` (ElementId): The MEP element the port belongs to.
- `name` (string, required)
- `position` (Coordinate3D, required)
- `direction` (Coordinate3D, required)
- `shape` (string, required)
- `width` (number, required)
- `height` (number, required)
- `domain` (MEPDomainOrUnknown, required)
- `mepSystemId` (AttributeId, required)
- `isPhysicallyConnected` (boolean): Whether the port is physically connected to another port. Available from Archicad 28.
- `isConnected` (boolean): Whether the port is connected to another port. Archicad 27 only; from Archicad 28 see isPhysicallyConnected.
- `connectionStyle` (MEPConnectionStyle): The connection style of the port. Available from Archicad 30.
- `flowDirection` (MEPFlowDirection): The flow direction of a piping or ventilation port.
- `nominalSize` (string): The nominal size of a piping port. Available from Archicad 30.
- `outerDiameter` (number): The outer diameter of a piping port.
- `wallThickness` (number): The wall thickness of a piping or ventilation port.
- `flangeSize` (number): The flange size of a piping or ventilation port. Available from Archicad 30.
- `connectedPortId` (Guid)
- `connectedElementId` (ElementId)

### MEPElementPorts

object: The ports of an MEP element.
- `ports` (array of MEPPortDetails, required)

### MEPElementPortsOrError

MEPElementPorts or ErrorItem: The ports of an MEP element or an error.

### MEPElementPortsOrErrors

array of MEPElementPortsOrError: A list of MEP element ports or errors.

### MEPFlexibleSegmentPolyline

array of object: The geometry of a polyline MEP flexible segment: its line and spline parts in order, which alternate and connect at their ends. Available from Archicad 28.

### MEPConnectionResult

object: The result of connecting an MEP routing element: the routing element deleted by merging, the routing element created by splitting and the branch element created by the connection. Empty in Archicad 27, which does not report them.
- `deletedRoutingElementId` (ElementId)
- `splitRoutingElementId` (ElementId)
- `createdBranchId` (ElementId)

### MEPConnectionResultOrError

MEPConnectionResult or ErrorItem: The result of an MEP connection or an error.

### MEPConnectionResultsOrErrors

array of MEPConnectionResultOrError: A list of MEP connection results or errors.

object: The fields to change, named as in the response of GetViewOptions. Fields not given keep their current value. Without an index, the window then uses Custom model view options (index 0), also when only on-screen view options are given. To keep the combination, give its index as well.

### AddOnViewpointDetails

object
- `viewpointId` (object, required): The identifier of the add-on viewpoint item.
  - `guid` (Guid, required)
- `parentViewpointId` (object): The identifier of the root or group the item is in. Missing when Archicad reports no parent, as for a root.
  - `guid` (Guid, required)
- `itemType` (string ("Root", "Group", "Leaf", "Undefined"), required): Whether the item is a root, a group or a leaf node.
- `displayId` (string, required): The ID shown for the item in the Project Map.
- `displayName` (string, required): The name shown for the item in the Project Map.
- `viewSettingsFlags` (integer, required): The view settings flags of the item, as Archicad stores them (a bit field).
- `data` (string, required): The data the add-on attached to the item, base64 encoded. Empty when there is none.

### AddOnViewpointType

string ("Root", "Group", "Leaf"): Whether to create a root, a group or a leaf node. Roots and groups can't be created in a Teamwork project.

  - `guid` (Guid, required)

- `displayName` (string): The name shown for the item in the Project Map.
- `viewSettingsFlags` (integer): The view settings flags of the item, as Archicad stores them (a bit field).
- `data` (string): Data to attach to the item, base64 encoded. It replaces the attached data; an empty string removes it.

### PlaceSettingsUpdate

object: The place settings to change (API_PlaceInfo), with its field names. Only the given keys are changed; an empty object changes nothing and returns the current settings.
- `longitude` (number): Longitude in degrees.
- `latitude` (number): Latitude in degrees.
- `altitude` (number): Altitude in meters.
- `north` (number): The north direction in radians.
- `year` (integer)
- `month` (integer)
- `day` (integer)
- `hour` (integer)
- `minute` (integer)
- `second` (integer)
- `sumTime` (boolean): Whether summer time (+1 hour) is on.
- `timeZoneInMinutes` (integer): The time zone, in minutes from Greenwich.
- `timeZoneOffset` (integer): Tells apart time zones with the same timeZoneInMinutes.

### UnitValueConversionData

object
- `value` (number, required): The value to convert, in meters, square meters, cubic meters or radians, matching the kind of the preference.
- `preference` (string ("WorkModel", "WorkLayout", "WorkAngle", "DimLinear", "DimAngle", "DimRadial", "DimLevel", "DimElevation", "DimDoorWindow", "DimParapet", "DimArea", "CalcLength", ...), required): The Project Preference whose unit and rounding are applied: WorkModel, WorkLayout and WorkAngle are the Working Units; the Dim ones are the Dimensions (DimDoorWindow the door, window and skylight dimensions, DimParapet the sill height, DimArea the area calculations); the Calc ones are the Calculation Units & Rules.

- `unit` (string, required): The unit of the preference. It may be empty.

### SetGDLParameterArray

array of SetGDLParameterDetails: The list of GDL parameters.

### GDLParameterArray

array of GDLParameterDetails: The list of GDL parameters.

### GDLParameterList

object: The list of GDL parameters.
- `parameters` (GDLParameterArray, required)

### PossibleStringValues

array of string: The possible string values of a GDL parameter.

### PossibleNumericValues

array of object: The possible numeric values of a GDL parameter.

### GDLParameterDetails

object: Details of a GDL parameter.
- `name` (string, required): The name of the parameter.
- `displayName` (string, required): The display name of the parameter.
- `index` (integer, required): The index of the parameter.
- `type` (string, required): The type of the parameter.
- `dimension1` (integer): The 1st dimension of array (in case of array value).
- `dimension2` (integer): The 2nd dimension of array (in case of array value).
- `value` (any, required): The value of the parameter. For an array parameter it is a flat list of all items row by row: dimension1 rows of dimension2 items each. SetGDLParametersOfElements accepts the same flat list back.
- `valueDescription` (string): The value description for numeric parameter.
- `isLocked` (boolean, required): The parameter is locked; i.e. the user cannot modify it
- `flags` (array of string ("Hidden", "HiddenFromScript", "Disabled", "Child", "Unique", "Fixed", "BoldName", "Open"), required): The flags of the parameter.
- `possibleValues` (PossibleStringValues or PossibleNumericValues)
- `canHaveCustomValue` (boolean): The parameter can have a custom value.
- `itemDescriptions` (array of string): Per-item text labels for an array-type parameter (API_AddParType.arrayDescriptions), one per array element in dim1xdim2 order. Only present when the library part defines them.

### SetGDLParameterByNameDetails

object: Details of a GDL parameter.
- `name` (string, required): The name of the parameter.
- `index1` (integer): Optional 1-based first index for changing a single item of an array parameter. Only valid for array parameters and only together with a single (non-list) value.
- `index2` (integer): Optional 1-based second index for changing a single item of a two-dimensional array parameter. Only valid together with index1. Defaults to 1.
- `value` (any, required): The new value of the parameter, in the unit GetGDLParametersOfElements reports it in (Angle parameters in radians). For array parameters provide a list of values for one-dimensional arrays (e.g. [1, 2, 3]) or a list of lists for two-dimensional arrays (e.g. [[11, 12], [21, 22]]); the list must contain exactly as many values as the parameter has items, resizing an array parameter is not supported. A two-dimensional array can also be given as a flat list of all its dimension1 x dimension2 items row by row, the layout GetGDLParametersOfElements returns. Alternatively provide index1 (and optionally index2) together with a single value to change one item of the array. Within one command call whole-array (list) values are applied after all single-value changes.

### SetGDLParameterByIndexDetails

object: Details of a GDL parameter.
- `index` (integer, required): The index of the parameter.
- `index1` (integer): Optional 1-based first index for changing a single item of an array parameter. Only valid for array parameters and only together with a single (non-list) value.
- `index2` (integer): Optional 1-based second index for changing a single item of a two-dimensional array parameter. Only valid together with index1. Defaults to 1.
- `value` (any, required): The new value of the parameter, in the unit GetGDLParametersOfElements reports it in (Angle parameters in radians). For array parameters provide a list of values for one-dimensional arrays (e.g. [1, 2, 3]) or a list of lists for two-dimensional arrays (e.g. [[11, 12], [21, 22]]); the list must contain exactly as many values as the parameter has items, resizing an array parameter is not supported. A two-dimensional array can also be given as a flat list of all its dimension1 x dimension2 items row by row, the layout GetGDLParametersOfElements returns. Alternatively provide index1 (and optionally index2) together with a single value to change one item of the array. Within one command call whole-array (list) values are applied after all single-value changes.

### SetGDLParameterDetails

SetGDLParameterByNameDetails or SetGDLParameterByIndexDetails

### MorphPolygonHole

object
- `vertexIds` (array of integer, required)

### BeamHoleType

string ("Rectangular", "Circular")

### MorphPolygon

object
- `vertexIds` (array of integer, required): Counterclockwise outer-loop vertex indices for this face.
- `filled` (boolean): Defaults to true. Set to false to create only this loop's edges (a wireframe outline, e.g. a bare rectangle with no surface fill) without an actual face - holes/surfaceId are ignored in that case, since there is no fill for them to apply to.
- `holes` (array of MorphPolygonHole): Optional hole loops cut out of this face, each a clockwise list of vertex indices.
- `surfaceId` (AttributeId): Optional per-face surface (render material) override. Uses the Morph's default surface when omitted. Ignored during creation in Archicad 25.

### MeshSubline

object
- `coordinates` (array of Coordinate3D, required): The 3D coordinates of the leveling subline of the mesh.

### CurtainWallPattern

object: The column (primary) or row (secondary) pattern of a curtain wall segment: the sizes of the columns/rows of one pattern unit and how the unit is repeated along the segment.
- `sizes` (array of number, required): The sizes (widths of the columns or heights of the rows) of the pattern unit in meters, in order from the start of the segment or from the bottom. The unit is repeated to fill the segment.
- `logic` (CurtainWallPatternLogic)
- `origin` (CurtainWallPatternOrigin)
- `flexibleIndices` (array of integer): Zero-based indices of the columns/rows of the pattern unit that 'BestDivision' may stretch. When omitted, all of them are flexible. Ignored by 'FixedSizes'.

### CurtainWallPatternCell

object: The panel and frame classes of one cell of the pattern unit of a curtain wall segment. Panel classes are numbered as Archicad numbers them: 0 is no panel (the cell is left empty), 1 is the first panel class of the curtain wall (as listed in the Curtain Wall Settings, from the favorite or the tool defaults), 2 the second and so on. Frame classes: 0 is no frame (the cell is merged with its neighbour), 1 the Division frame, 2 the Corner frame, 3 the Boundary frame, 4 the first custom frame class of the curtain wall, 5 the second and so on. Fields not given keep the default assignment of the cell.
- `columnIndex` (integer, required): Zero-based column of the cell within the pattern unit, counted from the start of the segment.
- `rowIndex` (integer, required): Zero-based row of the cell within the pattern unit, counted from the bottom.
- `panelClassIndex` (integer): The panel class of the cell. 0 leaves the cell without a panel (Archicad keeps a hidden 'deleted panel' subelement there). With a crossing frame it is the class of the left (or lower) half; see rightPanelClassIndex for the other half.
- `rightPanelClassIndex` (integer): The panel class of the right (or upper) half of a cell with a crossing frame. Defaults to panelClassIndex.
- `leftFrameClassIndex` (integer): The frame class of the frame on the left edge of the cell (the grid line at the start of the column).
- `bottomFrameClassIndex` (integer): The frame class of the frame on the bottom edge of the cell (the grid line at the bottom of the row).
- `crossingFrameType` (CurtainWallCrossingFrameType)
- `crossingFrameClassIndex` (integer): The frame class of the diagonal frame of the cell. Only used when crossingFrameType is not 'None'.

- `holeId` (number, required)

### LinkToSettings

object: Mode of linking an element to its home story.
- `homeStoryDifference` (integer): Difference of the home story from the current story.
- `newCreationMode` (boolean): Controls home-story selection during element creation. If true, homeStoryDifference selects the home story relative to the current story and the element's absolute floor index is ignored. If false, the absolute floor index is used and Archicad fills homeStoryDifference. This is a creation instruction, not a persistent linking mode.

### CoverFillOrientation

object: Orientation/distortion of the floor plan cover fill.
- `type` (HatchOrientationType)
- `origo` (Coordinate2D): Origin of the fill relative to the project origin.
- `matrix00` (number): X component of the primary distortion (direction) vector - the cosine of the fill angle, if not distorted.
- `matrix10` (number): Y component of the primary distortion (direction) vector - the sine of the fill angle, if not distorted.
- `matrix01` (number): X component of the secondary distortion vector - the cosine of the normal vector's angle, if not distorted.
- `matrix11` (number): Y component of the secondary distortion vector - the sine of the normal vector's angle, if not distorted.
- `innerRadius` (number): Radius for circular fill distortion (type Centered only).

### ProfileEdgeOverride

object
- `edgeIndex` (integer, required)
- `pen` (integer)
- `isVisibleLine` (boolean)
- `isInnerLine` (boolean): Whether the edge is an inner line of the profile (GetProfiles' edges[].isInnerLine).
- `isCutEndLine` (boolean): Whether the edge is a cut end line of the profile (GetProfiles' edges[].isCutEndLine).
- `lineTypeId` (AttributeIdArrayItem)
- `buildingMaterialId` (AttributeIdArrayItem)

object

- `polygonArcs` (array of PolyArc): Optional arcs along this contour's edges. begIndex/endIndex are 0-based positions within this contour's own polygonCoordinates.

### LineSymbolItemData

object
- `itemType` (string, required): Separator, CenterDot, CenterLine, Dot, RightAngle, Parallel, Line, Circle, or Arc.
- `centerOffset` (number): Vertical distance from the origin. Used for Separator, CenterDot, and CenterLine item types.
- `length` (number): Length of the item. Used for CenterLine, RightAngle, and Parallel item types.
- `begPos` (Coordinate2D): Beginning position. Used for Dot, RightAngle, Parallel, Line, Circle, and Arc item types.
- `endPos` (Coordinate2D): End position. Used for Line item type only.
- `radius` (number): Radius. Used for Circle and Arc item types.
- `beginAngle` (number): Beginning angle in radians, measured from the vertical axis. Used for Arc item type only.
- `endAngle` (number): End angle in radians, measured from the vertical axis. Used for Arc item type only.

### PenData

object
- `index` (integer, required): Index of the pen [1..255].
- `color` (ColorRGB)
- `width` (number): Thickness of the pen defined in paper millimeters.
- `description` (string): Textual description of the pen.

### ProfileSkinData

object: One new skin (hatch). Its shape is one or more closed polygon contours: the first is the outer boundary, any further ones are holes cut out of it - the same polygon+holes convention as e.g. CreateSlabs' polygonCoordinates/polygonArcs/holes, just expressed as a list of contours instead of a separate holes array.
- `contours` (array of ProfileSkinContour, required): Closed polygon contours forming this skin's cross-section, in the Profile's local coordinate system. Each contour is closed automatically - do not repeat its first vertex at the end.
- `buildingMaterialId` (AttributeIdArrayItem)
- `surfaceId` (AttributeIdArrayItem)
- `fillId` (AttributeIdArrayItem)
- `contourPen` (integer)
- `contourLineTypeId` (AttributeIdArrayItem)
- `isCore` (boolean)
- `isFinish` (boolean)
- `visibleCutEndLines` (boolean)
- `cutEndLinePen` (integer)
- `cutEndLineTypeId` (AttributeIdArrayItem)
- `edgeOverrides` (array of ProfileEdgeOverride): Per-edge pen/visibility/line type, targeted by 0-based edge index. Edge indices follow the same order as this skin's contours/polygonCoordinates: the outer contour's edges first (one edge per vertex, wrapping around), then each hole's, in the order the contours were given. Verify exact indices for a created skin via a follow-up GetProfiles call's skins[].edges before relying on them.

### PolyArc

object: Representation of an arc segment of a two dimensional polygon/polyline.
- `begIndex` (integer, required): Node index of one end point of the arc.
- `endIndex` (integer, required): Node index of the other end point of the arc.
- `arcAngle` (number, required): Angle of the arc; it is positive, if the arc is on the right-hand side of the straight segment.

### SnapFilter

object: Which points and lines of the elements the cursor snaps to while the designer clicks (Archicad's neig filter). Without it, the cursor snaps as usual.
- `base` (string ("All", "None", "Edges", "Nodes")): What the cursor snaps to before include and exclude are applied: All = everything, None = nothing, Edges = only the lines and edges of the elements, Nodes = only their points (end points, vertices, hotspots). Default: None when include is given, otherwise All.
- `include` (array of SnapType): The cursor also snaps to these.
- `exclude` (array of SnapType): The cursor does not snap to these. Applied after include.

### SnapType

string ("Wall", "WallOn", "Column", "ColumnOn", "Beam", "BeamOn", "Window", "WindowOn", "Door", "DoorOn", "Object", "ObjectOn", ...): A kind of point or line the cursor can snap to. An element type name means the element's points (end points, vertices, corners, hotspots); with On it means its lines and edges (for walls the reference line). Hotspot is a hotspot element, Text the corners of a text, Label the points of a label, Dimension a dimension point and DimensionOn the dimension line.

### InputConstraint

object: Archicad's drawing constraint for the clicks of a Get...FromUser command: the cursor can only move along it, as when a coordinate is locked in the Tracker. It is dissolved when the command returns, also on Escape and on errors.
- `type` (string ("X", "Y", "Z", "Angle", "Distance"), required): What is fixed: X = the X coordinate, Y = the Y coordinate, Z = the Z coordinate (3D window), Angle = the direction from the reference point (the cursor moves along a line), Distance = the distance from the reference point (the cursor moves along a circle).
- `value` (number, required): The fixed value: a coordinate or distance in meters, or for Angle an angle in radians, counterclockwise from the X axis.
- `fromLastPoint` (boolean): If true, the value is measured from the last clicked point (Archicad's local origin), otherwise from the project origin.

### Coordinate2D

object: 2D coordinate.
- `x` (number, required): X value of the coordinate.
- `y` (number, required): Y value of the coordinate.

### Coordinate3D

object: 3D coordinate.
- `x` (number, required): X value of the coordinate.
- `y` (number, required): Y value of the coordinate.
- `z` (number, required): Z value of the coordinate.

### CoordinateSystem3D

object: A coordinate system in 3D: an origin and three axes. What is left out keeps its default; give all three axes together or none.
- `origin` (Coordinate3D): The origin of the coordinate system.
- `xAxis` (Coordinate3D): The X axis of the coordinate system.
- `yAxis` (Coordinate3D): The Y axis of the coordinate system.
- `zAxis` (Coordinate3D): The Z axis of the coordinate system.

### ShellEdgeTrim

object: How a shell edge is cut.
- `trimType` (string ("Vertical", "Perpendicular", "Horizontal", "CustomAngle"), required): Vertical, Perpendicular or Horizontal to the shell, or at 'angle' (CustomAngle).
- `angle` (number): The trim angle in radians. Only CustomAngle uses it; pi/2 by default.

### RoofEdgeTrim

object: How an edge of a single-plane roof's polygon is cut (the edge's cut in the roof's settings).
- `trimType` (string ("Vertical", "Perpendicular", "Horizontal", "CustomAngle", "AlignWithCut")): Vertical, Perpendicular to the roof plane, Horizontal, or at 'angle' (CustomAngle). AlignWithCut is only reported, for shell edges; it cannot be written to a roof.
- `angle` (number): The angle of the edge cut in radians, as Archicad stores it. Only CustomAngle uses it.

### ShellProfile

object: A profile polyline of a shell, in the XY plane of its coordinate system.
- `coordinates` (array of Coordinate2D, required): The points of the polyline.
- `arcs` (array of PolyArc): Arc segments of the polyline, with indices into coordinates; index len(coordinates) is the first point again, which closes the polyline.
- `closed` (boolean): Whether the segment from the last point back to the first one is part of the profile. False by default.

### ShellCutPolygon

object: A closed polygon cutting a shell: its clipping contour or a hole.
- `coordinates` (array of Coordinate2D, required): The points of the polygon, in the XY plane of 'plane'.
- `arcs` (array of PolyArc): Arc segments of the polygon, with indices into coordinates.
- `plane` (CoordinateSystem3D): The plane of the polygon, in the coordinates of the shell's base plane: a hole is extruded from it along its Z axis. The base plane itself by default.
- `depth` (number): Required for holes, ignored for the clipping contour: how far the cutting body is extruded from the polygon's plane, along its Z axis (negative values cut downwards).

### AxonometryProjectionType

string ("YZ", "XZ", "XY", "Frontal", "Monometric", "Isometric", "Dimetric", "Bottom", "FrontalBottom", "MonometricBottom", "IsometricBottom", "DimetricBottom", ...): The projection type of an axonometric 3D projection, the projMod of the Archicad API. Archicad works out the transformation matrix of every type but Custom from the type and the azimuth. XY is the top view and Bottom the view from below. YZ and XZ are both the side view (an elevation), looking from the azimuth. Frontal, Monometric, Isometric and Dimetric are the predefined axonometries, and FrontalBottom, MonometricBottom, IsometricBottom and DimetricBottom the same seen from below; an Isometric at azimuth 270 is the isometric from the south-east (X axis at -30 degrees, Y at 30, Z at 90). Custom keeps the transformation matrix as given. Parallel cannot be set: Archicad makes it Custom.

### PerspectiveProjectionParameters

object: The parameters of a perspective projection of the 3D window.
- `cameraPosition` (Coordinate3D, required): The position of the camera.
- `targetPosition` (Coordinate3D, required): The position of the target point the camera looks at.
- `distance` (number, required): The distance between the camera and the target.
- `azimuth` (number, required): The azimuth of the camera in degrees: the direction from the target to the camera, counterclockwise from the X axis. Archicad works it out from the camera and target positions, so a set value is replaced by that.
- `viewCone` (number, required): The view cone angle of the camera in degrees.
- `rollAngle` (number, required): The roll angle of the camera.
- `isTwoPointPersp` (boolean, required): True for a two-point perspective (vertical edges stay vertical).
- `sun` (ProjectionSunSettings): The sun position of the perspective. Get3DProjectionSettings always returns it; Set3DProjectionSettings changes only the values given and keeps the current sun when it is missing.

### ProjectionSunSettings

object: The sun position of a 3D projection, the Sun Position of the 3D Projection Settings dialog (API_SunAngleSettings). Each perspective and axonometry has its own, independent of the project's date and time (SetSunSettings). The 3D shading and shadows of the projection come from it.
- `sunPositionOption` (string ("Angles", "DateAndTime")): Angles: the sun is at sunAzimuth and sunAltitude. DateAndTime: Archicad calculates the sun from the project location and the date and time given here.
- `sunAzimuth` (number): The azimuth of the sun, used when sunPositionOption is Angles. In the same units Get3DProjectionSettings returns it.
- `sunAltitude` (number): The altitude of the sun, used when sunPositionOption is Angles. In the same units Get3DProjectionSettings returns it.
- `year` (integer): Used when sunPositionOption is DateAndTime. 0 when no date is set.
- `month` (integer): Used when sunPositionOption is DateAndTime. 0 when no date is set.
- `day` (integer): Used when sunPositionOption is DateAndTime. 0 when no date is set.
- `hour` (integer)
- `minute` (integer)
- `second` (integer)
- `summerTime` (boolean): True when the time is daylight saving time.

### Dimensions3D

object: Dimensions in 3D.
- `x` (number, required): X dimension.
- `y` (number, required): Y dimension.
- `z` (number, required): Z dimension.

### ColorRGB

object: RGB color.
- `red` (number, required): Red value between 0.0 and 1.0
- `green` (number, required): Green value between 0.0 and 1.0
- `blue` (number, required): Blue value between 0.0 and 1.0

### Texture

object: Texture parameters
- `name` (string, required): The filename of the texture in the library (without extension).
- `rotationAngle` (number): Rotation angle in radians.
- `xSize` (number): X size of the picture in model space, by default 1.
- `ySize` (number): Y size of the picture in model space, by default 1.
- `FillRectangle` (boolean): True, if fit the rectangle with the picture in a central position, using the natural aspect ratio of the picture.
- `FitPicture` (boolean): True, if fit the picture in the middle of the rectangle, using the natural aspect ratio of the picture.
- `mirrorX` (boolean): True, if the texture is mirrored in X direction.
- `mirrorY` (boolean): True, if the texture is mirrored in Y direction.
- `useAlphaChannel` (boolean): True, if the alpha channel of the texture is used.
- `alphaChannelChangesTransparency` (boolean): True, if the alpha channel of the texture changes the transparency.
- `alphaChannelChangesSurfaceColor` (boolean): True, if the alpha channel of the texture changes the surface color.
- `alphaChannelChangesAmbientColor` (boolean): True, if the alpha channel of the texture changes the ambient color.
- `alphaChannelChangesSpecularColor` (boolean): True, if the alpha channel of the texture changes the specular color.
- `alphaChannelChangesDiffuseColor` (boolean): True, if the alpha channel of the texture changes the diffuse color.

### Error

object: The details of an error.
- `code` (integer, required): The code of the error.
- `message` (string, required): The error message.

### ErrorItem

object
- `error` (Error, required)

### OverriddenValue

object: A value the active graphic override combination may replace. 'overridden' tells whether it does; only then the value is given: 'attributeId' for line types, fills and surfaces, 'penIndex' for pens, 'color' for background pens and surfaces set to a color.
- `overridden` (boolean, required)
- `attributeId` (AttributeId)
- `penIndex` (integer)
- `color` (object)
  - `red` (number, required)
  - `green` (number, required)
  - `blue` (number, required)

### SuccessfulExecutionResult

object: The result of a successful execution.
- `success` (boolean (true), required)

### FailedExecutionResult

object: The result of a failed execution.
- `success` (boolean (false), required)
- `error` (Error, required)

### ExecutionResult

SuccessfulExecutionResult or FailedExecutionResult: The result of the execution.

### ExecutionResults

array of ExecutionResult: A list of execution results.

### DryRun

boolean: If true, the command makes all the checks of a real run and resolves the same targets, with the same errors, but changes nothing in the project and creates no undo step. The response is that of a real run with "dryRun": true added, and says for each target what the real run would do. Default is false.

### DryRunFlag

boolean (true): Present, and true, only in the response of a dry run (the dryRun input was true): nothing was changed in the project.

### WouldDeleteExecutionResult

object: The result of a dry run for a target that passed every check: a real run would delete it.
- `success` (boolean (true), required)
- `wouldDelete` (boolean (true), required)

### DeletionExecutionResult

SuccessfulExecutionResult or WouldDeleteExecutionResult or FailedExecutionResult: The result of a deletion for one target. On a dry run a target that passed every check gets wouldDelete instead of being deleted.

### DeletionExecutionResults

array of DeletionExecutionResult: A list of deletion results.

### WouldChange

object: What a real run would change on a target. Each command says what its oldValue and newValue are; either is left out when it cannot be told cheaply.
- `oldValue` (any): The target's value now, before the change.
- `newValue` (any): The value a real run would write.

### WouldChangeExecutionResult

object: The result of a dry run for a target that passed every check: a real run would change it as wouldChange says.
- `success` (boolean (true), required)
- `wouldChange` (WouldChange, required)

### ChangeExecutionResult

SuccessfulExecutionResult or WouldChangeExecutionResult or FailedExecutionResult: The result of a change for one target. On a dry run a target that passed every check gets wouldChange instead of being changed.

### ChangeExecutionResults

array of ChangeExecutionResult: A list of change results.

### ElementCategoryType

string ("StructuralFunction", "Position", "RenovationStatus", "RenovationFilter", "BRI"): The type of an element category. The names of the categories and of their values are localized, so scripts should select a category by this type and a value by its categoryValueId, never by name. BRI is available only in the German localized version of Archicad.

### ElementCategoryValueId

object: The identifier of a value of an element category.
- `guid` (Guid, required)

### ElementCategoryId

object: The identifier of an element category.
- `guid` (Guid, required)

### ElementType

string ("Wall", "Column", "Beam", "Window", "Door", "Object", "Lamp", "Slab", "Roof", "Mesh", "Dimension", "RadialDimension", ...): The type of an element.

### ElementFilter

string ("IsEditable", "IsVisibleByLayer", "IsVisibleByRenovation", "IsVisibleByStructureDisplay", "IsVisibleIn3D", "OnActualFloor", "OnActualLayout", "InMyWorkspace", "IsIndependent", "InCroppedView", "HasAccessRight", "IsOverriddenByRenovation", ...): A filter type for an element. Note: elements hidden by the design option combination of the current view (Archicad 29 or newer) fail IsVisibleByRenovation and pass IsOverriddenByRenovation even when the project has no renovation filter; use GetDesignOptionForElements and GetDesignOptionCombinationOfViews to tell them apart.

### ElementTypeFloorLayerFilter

object: A server-side element filter. An element matches when its type, its home story and its layer are each among the listed ones; an omitted or empty list does not filter.
- `types` (array of ElementType): Element types to keep (e.g. ['Wall', 'Column']).
- `floorIndices` (array of integer): Home story indices to keep (e.g. [0, 1]).
- `layerIndices` (array of integer): Layer attribute indices to keep.

### WindowType

string ("FloorPlan", "Section", "Details", "3DModel", "Layout", "Drawing", "CustomText", "CustomDraw", "MasterLayout", "Elevation", "InteriorElevation", "Worksheet", ...): The type of a window.

### NavigatorItemIdOrDatabaseIdAndWindowType

NavigatorItemIdArrayItem or DatabaseIdAndWindowType: Identifies the window to change to. Either a navigatorItemId on its own (the navigator item's saved view settings are applied), or a windowType optionally narrowed to a specific databaseId, or a databaseId on its own (its window type is resolved automatically).

### DisplayOption

string ("Standard", "StandardWithAbstract", "CutOnly", "OutLinesOnly", "AbstractAll", "CutAll"): Floor plan display option.

### ViewDepthLimitation

string ("ToFloorPlanRange", "ToAbsoluteLimit", "EntireElement"): Floor plan view depth limitation.

### ElemProjectionMode

string ("Symbolic", "Projected", "Hybrid"): Floor plan projection mode of an element part (API_ElemProjectionModesID).

### TextureProjectionType

string ("Invalid", "Planar", "Default", "Cylindric", "Spheric", "Box"): Projection type of the 3D texture.

### MeshRidges

string ("AllSharp", "AllSmooth", "UserDefined"): How ridges between mesh facets are displayed in 3D: 'AllSharp' shows all ridges, 'AllSmooth' hides them, 'UserDefined' shows only ridges along user-defined level lines (the drawing-set look for contour-line topography).

### CurtainWallPatternLogic

string ("FixedSizes", "BestDivision"): How the pattern unit fills the segment: 'FixedSizes' keeps the given sizes and repeats the unit, which may leave a partial unit at the end (Archicad: Fixed Size); 'BestDivision' stretches the flexible columns/rows so that whole units fill the segment with the least stretching (Archicad: Best Division).

### CurtainWallPatternOrigin

string ("StartWithPattern", "StartFromCenter", "AlignToCenter", "EndWithPattern"): Where the pattern unit is anchored on the segment: at its start, centered with a unit starting at the center, centered with a unit centered on the center, or at its end.

### CurtainWallCrossingFrameType

string ("None", "FromBottomLeftToTopRight", "FromTopLeftToBottomRight"): The diagonal frame of a pattern cell: none, or from the bottom left to the top right corner, or from the top left to the bottom right corner.

### BeamAnchorPoint

string ("TopLeft", "TopCenter", "TopRight", "MiddleLeft", "Center", "MiddleRight", "BottomLeft", "BottomCenter", "BottomRight"): Anchor point of the beam cross section on a 3x3 grid.

### ColumnCoreAnchor

string ("TopLeft", "TopCenter", "TopRight", "MiddleLeft", "Center", "MiddleRight", "BottomLeft", "BottomCenter", "BottomRight"): Anchor point of the column core on a 3x3 grid.

### SlabReferencePlaneLocation

string ("Top", "CoreTop", "CoreBottom", "Bottom"): Location of the slab reference plane.

### WallReferenceLineLocation

string ("Outside", "Center", "Inside", "CoreOutside", "CoreCenter", "CoreInside"): The Core* values only have an effect on a Composite or Profile wall (structureType) - a Basic wall has no core skin, and Archicad falls back to the nearest non-core equivalent (e.g. CoreCenter becomes Center).

### WallZoneRelation

string ("Boundary", "ReduceArea", "None", "SubtractFromZone")

### WallGeometryType

string ("Straight", "Trapezoid", "Polygonal")

### WallModificationGeometryType

string ("Straight", "Trapezoid"): The wall's plan outline shape, distinct from its cross section shape.

### WallProfileType

string ("Normal", "Slanted", "Trapez", "Poly"): Cross section shape of the wall, distinct from geometryType (which is the plan outline).

### WallModificationProfileType

string ("Normal", "Slanted", "Trapez"): Cross section shape of the wall, distinct from geometryType (which is the plan outline).

### IFCElementsToExport

string ("EntireProject", "VisibleElementsOnAllStories", "AllElementsOnCurrentStory", "VisibleElementsOnCurrentStory", "SelectedElementsOnly"): Which elements to export.

### ClassificationSystemConflictPolicy

string ("merge", "replace", "skip"): What to do with a system whose name already exists: merge, replace it, or keep the existing one.

### ClassificationItemConflictPolicy

string ("replace", "skip"): What to do with an item whose id already exists in a merged system: replace it or keep the existing one.

### PropertyImportConflictPolicy

string ("append", "replace", "skip"): What to do with a property whose name already exists in its group: append imports it under a new unused name, replace replaces the existing definition, skip keeps the existing one.

### DesignOptionLinkType

string ("NotExistingElement", "MissingDesignOption", "NotLinkedToAnyDesignOption", "LinkedToDesignOption"): The type of the associated design option.

### MEPDomain

string ("Ventilation", "Piping", "CableCarrier"): The MEP domain.

### MEPDomainOrUnknown

string ("Ventilation", "Piping", "CableCarrier", "Unknown"): The reported MEP domain. Unknown indicates that the domain could not be determined.

### MEPElementType

string ("RoutingElement", "RigidSegment", "Elbow", "Transition", "Branch", "Terminal", "Accessory", "Equipment", "Fitting", "FlexibleSegment", "TakeOff", "ElectricalPanel", ...)

### DrawingNameType

string ("ViewOrSourceFileName", "ViewIdAndName", "CustomName"): How the drawing's title name is assembled (Identification tabpage of the Drawing Settings dialog).

### DrawingNumberingType

string ("ByLayout", "ByViewId", "CustomNumber"): How the drawing's title ID is assigned (Identification tabpage of the Drawing Settings dialog).

### DrawingPenTableUsageMode

string ("OwnPenTable", "ModelPenTable", "PenTableIndex"): Which pen table the drawing uses (API_DrawingType::penTableUsageMode): its own, the one of the model, or the pen set given by penTableIndex.

### DrawingColorMode

string ("OriginalColors", "BlackAndWhite", "Grayscale"): How the drawing's pens are output (API_DrawingType::colorMode).

### DrawingAnchorPoint

string ("TopLeft", "TopCenter", "TopRight", "MiddleLeft", "Center", "MiddleRight", "BottomLeft", "BottomCenter", "BottomRight"): The node of the drawing's bounding box the drawing is placed by (API_DrawingType::anchorPoint). Used only when useOwnOriginAsAnchor is false.

### DrawingStatus

string ("UpToDate", "Modified", "Unknown"): The Drawing Manager's Status column: UpToDate (OK) when the drawing matches its source, Modified when the source changed since the drawing was last updated, Unknown when the status cannot be determined (e.g. a missing external source).

### DrawingLinkType

string ("InternalView", "ExternalView", "Drawing", "DXF_DWG", "PDF", "Image", "PlotMaker", "AddOn", "Unknown", "Other"): The kind of source a drawing is linked to (the Drawing Manager's Source column): a view of this project (InternalView), a view of another Archicad project file (ExternalView), a drawing file, a DWG/DXF file, a PDF, an image, a PlotMaker file, an Add-On generated drawing, or an unknown/other source.

### MEPCrossSectionShape

string ("Rectangular", "Circular", "Oval", "UShape"): Shape of an MEP routing segment's cross section or of an MEP port.

### MEPConnectionStyle

string ("SimpleBody", "Flanged", "Welded"): How the pieces of an MEP routing segment, or an MEP port, are connected. For pipes, the settings dialog of Archicad 29 shows SimpleBody as Welded, and Welded is refused on a pipe route.

### MEPFlowDirection

string ("FlowNotDefined", "FlowIn", "FlowOut"): The flow direction of a piping or ventilation port.

### MEPPreferredTransitionPlacement

string ("SmallToLarge", "LargeToSmall"): Where an MEP routing node places its transitions.

### MEPCutPlanePosition

string ("AtUpperDisplayLimit", "ByViewSettings"): Where the floor plan cut plane of an MEP routing element is. Available from Archicad 29.

### MEPFloorPlanDisplayOption

string ("Projected", "ProjectedWithOverhead", "Symbolic", "ByMVO"): How an MEP routing element is shown on the floor plan. Available from Archicad 29.

### MEPShowProjection

string ("ToFloorPlanRange", "ToAbsoluteDisplayLimit", "EntireElement"): How much of an MEP routing element's projection is shown on the floor plan. Available from Archicad 29.

### MEPOnStoryVisibility

string ("AllRelevantStories", "HomeStoryOnly"): On which stories an MEP routing element is shown. Available from Archicad 29.

### MEPPortDefaultDetails

object: The settings of one port of an MEP tool default. Each field is present only where the port's domain and the Archicad version have it: Archicad 27 gives only the index and the shape.
- `index` (integer, required): The index of the port in the default.
- `domain` (MEPDomain)
- `name` (string)
- `shape` (MEPCrossSectionShape)
- `width` (number)
- `height` (number): The height of a ventilation or cable carrier port.
- `diameter` (number): The diameter of a piping port.
- `wallThickness` (number): The wall thickness of a piping or ventilation port.
- `flowDirection` (MEPFlowDirection): The flow direction of a piping or ventilation port.
- `flangeSize` (number): The flange size of a piping or ventilation port, when it has flanges. Available from Archicad 30.
- `connectionStyle` (MEPConnectionStyle): Available from Archicad 30.
- `mepSystemId` (AttributeId)

### MEPElementDefaultDetails

object: The settings of a terminal, accessory, fitting, equipment or branch tool default.
- `libraryPartId` (LibPartUnId, required): The library part the tool places.
- `insulationThickness` (number): The insulation thickness, when the default has insulation.
- `ports` (array of MEPPortDefaultDetails, required)

### MEPDomainToolDefaults

object: The current settings of the MEP tools of one domain. A tool whose default Archicad does not give for the domain is left out; a setting is left out where the Archicad version does not have it.
- `domain` (MEPDomain, required)
- `routingElement` (object): The routing tool default.
  - `mepSystemId` (AttributeId, required)
  - `branchPreferenceTableId` (Guid)
  - `cutPlanePosition` (MEPCutPlanePosition)
  - `floorPlanDisplayOption` (MEPFloorPlanDisplayOption)
  - `showProjection` (MEPShowProjection)
  - `onStoryVisibility` (MEPOnStoryVisibility)
  - `routingSegment` (object, required): The segment default of the routing tool.
  - `routingNode` (object, required): The node default of the routing tool.
- `rigidSegment` (object): The rigid segment default of the routing tool.
  - `shape` (MEPCrossSectionShape): Archicad 27 and 28.
  - `width` (number): Archicad 27 and 28.
  - `height` (number): Archicad 27 and 28.
  - `insulationThickness` (number): The insulation thickness, when the default has insulation.
- `branch` (MEPElementDefaultDetails): The branch default of the routing tool.
- `flexibleSegment` (object): The flexible segment tool default. Archicad 27 has it in the Ventilation domain only.
  - `shape` (MEPCrossSectionShape, required)
  - `width` (number, required)
  - `height` (number, required)
- `terminal` (MEPElementDefaultDetails)
- `accessory` (MEPElementDefaultDetails)
- `fitting` (MEPElementDefaultDetails)

### MEPPreferenceTableDomain

string ("Piping", "Ventilation", "CableCarrier")

### MEPPreferenceRowIndex

integer: The position of the row in its preference table, as ModifyMEPPreferenceTables expects it. Rows that cannot be read are left out of GetMEPPreferenceTables, so this is not always the position in the rows list.

### MEPPreferenceTableType

string ("Segment", "Elbow", "Branch", "Transition"): The kind of preference table container: the segment tables (circular and rectangular ducts share one container), or the elbow, branch or transition tables. CableCarrier has only segment tables, transition tables are available from Archicad 29.

### MEPPreferenceRowChange

object: Changes one row of a preference table, in the shape GetMEPPreferenceTables returns. Only the given values are changed. A value that does not belong to the kind of table is an error; the read-only values (reference ids, branchAxisAngle, isValid, and angle of an elbow table) are ignored.
- `index` (MEPPreferenceRowIndex, required)
- `delete` (boolean): Deletes the row. The circular segment tables, and the elbow tables in Archicad 28, have a fixed row for each reference id; there the row is emptied instead. Cannot be combined with new values.
- `diameter` (number): Circular segment and elbow tables.
- `wallThickness` (number): Circular segment tables.
- `value` (number): Rectangular duct and cable carrier segment tables. These tables keep their rows ordered by value, so a changed value can move the row; the indices of the other rows given in the same call are followed.
- `radius` (number): Elbow tables.
- `mainAxisDiameter` (number): Branch tables.
- `branchAxisDiameter` (number): Branch tables.
- `length` (number): Branch tables and piping transition tables.
- `branchOffset` (number): Branch tables.
- `connectionLength` (number): Branch tables.
- `beginDiameter` (number): Transition tables.
- `endDiameter` (number): Transition tables.
- `angle` (number): Ventilation transition tables, in the unit GetMEPPreferenceTables returns it. Read-only (ignored) in elbow tables.
- `description` (string)
- `referenceId` (integer): Read-only, ignored.
- `mainAxisReferenceId` (integer): Read-only, ignored.
- `branchAxisReferenceId` (integer): Read-only, ignored.
- `beginReferenceId` (integer): Read-only, ignored.
- `endReferenceId` (integer): Read-only, ignored.
- `branchAxisAngle` (number): Read-only, ignored.
- `isValid` (boolean): Read-only, ignored.

### MEPPreferenceTableChange

object: Changes one preference table, in the shape GetMEPPreferenceTables returns. Only the given values and rows are changed.
- `guid` (string, required): The guid of the table, as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTables.
- `name` (string): The new name of the table.
- `isEditable` (boolean): Read-only, ignored.
- `useIndividualSegmentLengths` (boolean): Segment tables only. Available from Archicad 29.
- `minimumSegmentationLength` (number): Segment tables only; the maximum is kept when not given. Available from Archicad 29.
- `maximumSegmentationLength` (number): Segment tables only; the minimum is kept when not given. Available from Archicad 29.
- `rows` (array of MEPPreferenceRowChange): The rows to change or delete, each at most once. All indices refer to the table before this call.
- `newRows` (array of object): Rows to add to a rectangular duct or cable carrier segment table, after the other changes. Adding rows to the other tables is not supported yet.
  - `value` (number, required)
  - `description` (string)

### AssociativeWitnessPoint

object: A witness point of a dimension. Give elementId (with line, inIndex, special, nodeType, nodeStatus and nodeId as needed) for a point associated with an element, or only coordinate for a static point that is not associated with any element, like a point added by hand on empty space. elementId together with coordinate gives an associative point at that location on the element.
- `elementId` (ElementId)
- `coordinate` (Coordinate2D): Without elementId: the position of a static (non-associative) witness point; the other fields are ignored for a static point. With elementId: the location of the associative point on the referenced element (written to its base location), e.g. where the dimension line crosses a long or oblique wall face; without it Archicad chooses the point, e.g. the middle of a wall edge. Whether Archicad keeps this location for every kind of base (edges with line true, or only hotspots) is not verified.
- `line` (boolean)
- `inIndex` (integer)
- `special` (integer)
- `nodeType` (integer)
- `nodeStatus` (integer)
- `nodeId` (number)

### IFCExportTranslator

object
- `name` (string, required): The name of the translator, as the IFC Translators dialog shows it.
- `preview` (boolean, required): Whether this is the first item of Archicad's translator list, which the Archicad API documents as the preview translator (the one the IFC properties of elements are previewed with). No API identifies the preview translator otherwise, and in some projects the IFC Translators dialog shows another translator as the preview one.

### CoordinateWitnessPoint

object
- `coordinate` (Coordinate2D)
- `coordinate3D` (Coordinate3D)
- `dimensionPosition` (Coordinate2D)
- `dimensionValue` (number)
- `witnessForm` (string ("None", "Small", "Large", "Fix", "Unknown"))
- `witnessVal` (number)
- `baseElementId` (ElementId)
- `line` (boolean): True when the witness point lies on an edge of the base element rather than at a node (API_Base line).
- `inIndex` (integer): Subindex of the base element's node (API_Neig inIndex).
- `special` (integer): Non-zero for special references such as a wall plane, a beam, window or door hole, or a mesh ridge (API_Base special).
- `nodeType` (integer): Reserved by Archicad for section dimensions (API_Base node_typ).
- `nodeStatus` (integer): Reserved by Archicad for section dimensions (API_Base node_status).
- `nodeId` (number): Polygon vertex id of the base element, from its memo's vertexIDs, for elements with a polygon.
- `textHeight` (number): Character height of the dimension text in mm, as the creation commands take it.
- `textPen` (integer): Pen index of the dimension text.
- `textFrame` (boolean): Whether the dimension text has a frame.

### InteriorElevationData

object
- `nodeCoordinates` (array of Coordinate2D, required): The corner points of the connected segment chain. Each consecutive pair of points becomes one segment, so a room with four walls needs five points to be closed, or four to be left open.
- `depth` (number): How far each segment looks. Applied to every segment. Defaults to 1.0.
- `name` (string): Name of the interior elevation. Each segment is named after it.
- `id` (string): ID string of the interior elevation.
- `floorIndex` (integer): The story to place the interior elevation on. Defaults to the current story.

### HotlinkInstanceChange

object
- `elementId` (ElementId, required)
- `origin` (HotlinkOrigin): If z is omitted, the instance's current z is kept.
- `rotationAngle` (number): Rotation about the origin, counter-clockwise, in radians.
- `mirrored` (boolean): Reflect the module's local X axis before the rotation.
- `floorDifference` (integer)
- `skipNested` (boolean)
- `suspendFixAngle` (boolean)
- `ignoreTopFloorLinks` (boolean)
- `relinkWallOpenings` (boolean)
- `adjustLevelDiffs` (boolean)
- `layerIndex` (integer): Move the instance to this layer. A layerIndex that is not a layer of the project is refused.

### HotlinkInstanceCreation

object
- `hotlinkNodeId` (HotlinkNodeId, required): The node to place, from GetHotlinks or CreateHotlinkNodes. On Archicad 25 a node that has never been placed cannot be read, so a node created through the API can only be placed from Archicad 26 on.
- `origin` (HotlinkOrigin, required): If z is omitted, the instance is placed at 0.
- `rotationAngle` (number): Optional rotation about the origin, counter-clockwise, in radians. Defaults to 0.
- `mirrored` (boolean): Optional. Reflects the module's local X axis before the rotation. Defaults to false.
- `floorIndex` (integer): Optional story the instance is placed on. Defaults to the current story.
- `floorDifference` (integer): Optional story offset applied to the module's stories. Defaults to the hotlink tool's current default.
- `layerIndex` (integer): Optional layer of the instance. Defaults to the hotlink tool's current default layer, or to the built-in Archicad layer when that layer has been deleted. A layerIndex that is not a layer of the project is refused.
- `skipNested` (boolean): Optional. Do not place hotlinks nested inside the module. Defaults to the hotlink tool's current default.
- `suspendFixAngle` (boolean): Optional. Rotate fixed-angle elements with the module. Defaults to the hotlink tool's current default.
- `ignoreTopFloorLinks` (boolean): Optional. Top-linked elements keep their height rather than their top story link. Defaults to the hotlink tool's current default.
- `relinkWallOpenings` (boolean): Optional. Defaults to the hotlink tool's current default.
- `adjustLevelDiffs` (boolean): Optional. Defaults to the hotlink tool's current default.

- `subVersion` (integer): The sub version of the package.
- `minArchicadVersion` (integer): The minimum Archicad version the package needs.
- `minArchicadBuildNumber` (integer): The minimum Archicad build number the package needs.
- `dependencies` (array of object): The packages this package depends on.
  - `name` (string, required): The name of the package.
  - `packageId` (string, required): The GUID of the package.
  - `version` (integer, required): The version of the package that is needed.

### PropertyDefinitionUpdate

object
- `propertyId` (PropertyId, required)
- `name` (string): New name of the property.
- `description` (string): New description of the property.
- `isEditable` (boolean): Whether users may edit the value of the property on elements (Property Manager: Editable).
- `groupId` (PropertyGroupId): Move the property into this custom property group.
- `defaultValue` (PropertyDefaultValue): New default value: a basic value or expressions. Switching between the two is allowed.
- `expressions` (array of string): The new expression strings for the property. Only for expression-based properties.
- `availability` (PropertyAvailabilityUpdate)
- `possibleEnumValues` (EnumValuesToAdd): Values already on the property keep their identifier, so element values assigned to them survive; values not listed here are kept as well.
- `renameEnumValues` (array of PropertyEnumValueRename): Change the text of existing enum options. The option keeps its identifier, so element values follow the new text.
- `removeEnumValues` (array of PropertyEnumValueRemoval): Enum options to remove. Elements holding a removed option lose that value.
- `enumOrder` (array of string): Every option's display text, once, in the new order (applied after rename, remove and add).

- `index` (integer, required): The index of the descriptor in the listing database set when status is Normal, in the library part when status is Local.
- `status` (ElementDescriptorStatus, required)

### ElementDescriptorStatus

string ("Normal", "Deleted", "Local", "Unknown"): Normal: the descriptor exists in the listing database. Deleted: it is referenced, but deleted from the database. Local: it is defined in the library part. Unknown for a value this version of Tapir does not name.

### Body3D

object: One solid body of an element's 3D model: a flat vertex list in world coordinates and the planar faces referencing it. The faces are not triangulated: a face is a closed loop of vertex indices (counterclockwise seen from outside the body) plus the loops of its holes.
- `vertices` (array of Coordinate3D, required): The vertices of the body in world coordinates (meters, absolute Z).
- `polygons` (array of object, required): The faces of the body.
  - `vertexIds` (array of integer, required): The outer contour of the face: 0-based indices into vertices.
  - `holes` (array of object): The holes in the face, each a closed loop of 0-based indices into vertices.
  - `surfaceId` (AttributeId): The surface attribute of the face. Left out when the face's material is not a project attribute (for example one defined by a GDL script).

### ViewSettings

object: The settings of a navigator view
- `modelViewOptions` (string): The name of the model view options. If empty, the view has custom model view options.
- `layerCombination` (string): The name of the layer combination. If empty, the view has custom layer combination.
- `dimensionStyle` (string): The name of the dimension style. If empty, the view has custom dimension style.
- `penSetName` (string): The name of the pen set. If empty, the view has custom pen set.
- `graphicOverrideCombination` (string): The name of the graphic override combination. If empty, the view has custom graphic override combination.
- `drawingScale` (integer): The drawing scale stored on the view, if enabled (see saveFlags.drawingScale). Giving it to SetViewSettings also turns saveFlags.drawingScale on, unless that flag is given explicitly.
- `saveZoom` (boolean): Whether the zoom box is stored in the view. The same flag as saveFlags.zoom, kept for compatibility; in SetViewSettings saveFlags.zoom wins when both are given.
- `ignoreSavedZoom` (boolean): Whether changing to the view should ignore its stored zoom.
- `zoom` (Zoom): Stored zoom box. Used only when saveZoom is true. Giving it to SetViewSettings also turns saveFlags.zoom on, unless that flag is given explicitly.
- `saveFlags` (object): Which settings the view stores: the "stored in this view" checkboxes of the View Settings dialog. A stored setting whose name field is empty is a custom (unnamed) one; a setting that is not stored is not part of the view at all, which the name fields alone cannot tell apart. Always complete in a GetViewSettings response. In SetViewSettings every flag is optional, a flag that is not given keeps its current value, and a flag given here overrides the one implied by drawingScale, zoom, structureDisplay or saveZoom.
  - `zoom` (boolean): Whether the zoom box is stored in the view.
  - `displayOptions` (boolean): Whether the model view options are stored in the view (named by modelViewOptions, custom if that is empty).
  - `layers` (boolean): Whether the layer settings are stored in the view (named by layerCombination, custom if that is empty).
  - `drawingScale` (boolean): Whether the drawing scale is stored in the view.
  - `dimensions` (boolean): Whether the dimension settings are stored in the view (named by dimensionStyle, custom if that is empty).
  - `penSet` (boolean): Whether the pen set is stored in the view (named by penSetName, custom if that is empty).
  - `structureDisplay` (boolean): Whether the structure display mode is stored in the view.
- `rotation` (number): View rotation angle in radians, derived from transformationMatrix. Read via GetViewSettings; use SetViewRotation to change it.
- `transformationMatrix` (array of number): The full 2D transformation of the view that rotation is derived from: the 3x4 matrix row by row (12 numbers), in the layout Get3DProjectionSettings uses. Its translation is at indices 3 and 7. Read via GetViewSettings; SetViewSettings ignores it, use rotation or SetViewRotation to change the rotation and translation to change the translation.
- `translation` (object): SetViewSettings only: the translation part of the view transformation (indices 3 and 7 of transformationMatrix), so that view coordinates = rotation applied to model coordinates + translation. rotation leaves the translation as it is; without this field the translation is not changed. {x: 0, y: 0} clears it. Never returned by GetViewSettings (read it from transformationMatrix).
  - `x` (number, required)
  - `y` (number, required)
- `structureDisplay` (string ("EntireStructure", "CoreOnly", "WithoutFinishes", "StructureOnly")): Structure display mode. One of EntireStructure, CoreOnly, WithoutFinishes, StructureOnly.
- `renovationFilterGuid` (GuidId): Identifier of the renovation filter applied to the view.
- `renovationFilterName` (string): Name of the renovation filter applied to the view. Read-only (GetViewSettings): present together with renovationFilterGuid when the name could be resolved; set the filter via renovationFilterGuid.
- `d3styleName` (string): Name of the 3D style. Empty if not set.
- `renderingSceneName` (string): Name of the rendering scene. Empty if not set.
- `usePhotoRendering` (boolean): Whether photo rendering is used for this view.

### WallDetails

object
- `geometryType` (WallGeometryType, required)
- `begCoordinate` (Coordinate2D, required)
- `endCoordinate` (Coordinate2D, required)
- `zCoordinate` (number, required)
- `flipped` (boolean)
- `height` (number, required): height relative to bottom
- `bottomOffset` (number, required): base level of the wall relative to the floor level
- `offset` (number, required): wall's base line's offset from ref. line
- `arcAngle` (number): The arc angle of the curved wall in radians.
- `begThickness` (number): Thickness at the beginning of wall, it will return 0 for poly wall type
- `endThickness` (number): Thickness at the end of wall, it will return 0 for poly wall type
- `polygonOutline` (array of Coordinate2D): Polygon outline in case of polygonal wall
- `polygonArcs` (array of PolyArc): Polygon arcs in case of polygonal wall
- `structureType` (WallStructureType)
- `buildingMaterialId` (AttributeId)
- `compositeId` (AttributeId)
- `profileId` (AttributeId)
- `referenceLineLocation` (WallReferenceLineLocation)
- `profileType` (WallProfileType): Only Normal/Slanted/Trapez are settable via ModifyWalls - Poly needs a profile attribute wired through a separate mechanism. slantAlpha/slantBeta only have an effect once this is Slanted or Trapez.
- `slantAlpha` (number): Only has an effect once profileType is set to Slanted or Trapez.
- `slantBeta` (number): Only has an effect once profileType is set to Slanted or Trapez.
- `topOffset` (number): Only has an effect when relativeTopStory is non-zero.
- `relativeTopStory` (number): Non-zero links the wall's top to another story instead of an explicit height - do not set together with 'height' via ModifyWalls in the same call.
- `zoneRel` (WallZoneRelation)
- `visibility` (StoryVisibility): On Archicad 29 a wall knows only 'Home story only' and 'All relevant stories' (Wall Settings offers no Custom option), so a wall can read back a combination the dialog cannot show - a wall fresh from the Wall tool defaults may report showOnHome false with showRelAbove 1, which Wall Settings shows as an empty Show on Stories field (#852). See ModifyWalls for which combinations can be written.
- `isAutoOnStoryVisibility` (boolean): When true (the default on a new wall), Archicad recomputes 'visibility' automatically from the wall's vertical extent and ignores any value set for it.
- `referenceMaterial` (OverriddenMaterial)
- `oppositeMaterial` (OverriddenMaterial)
- `sideMaterial` (OverriddenMaterial)
- `cutFillPen` (OverriddenPen)
- `cutFillBackgroundPen` (OverriddenPen)
- `contourPen` (integer): Pen of the wall's own contour/reference outline (API_WallType::contPen) - distinct from cutFillPen, which is the cut fill pattern's pen inherited from the building material/composite/profile. Unlike cutFillPen this is not inheritable/overridable, it is the wall's own pen index directly, the same field used regardless of structureType (Basic, Composite or Profile).
- `contourPen3D` (integer): Pen of the wall's contour in 3D views (API_WallType::contPen3D).
- `contourLineTypeId` (AttributeId): Line type of the wall's own contour (API_WallType::contLtype) - pairs with contourPen, which only sets the pen, not the line type.
- `belowViewLineTypeId` (AttributeId): Line type used when "OutLines Only" is selected from the "Floor Plan Display" popup (API_WallType::belowViewLineType). Corresponds to the "Uncut Lines" value in the Wall Settings dialog.
- `aboveViewLinePen` (integer): Pen used when "Overhead All" is selected from the "Floor Plan Display" popup. Corresponds to the "Overhead Line Pens" value in the Wall Settings dialog.
- `aboveViewLineTypeId` (AttributeId): Line type used when "Overhead All" is selected from the "Floor Plan Display" popup - pairs with aboveViewLinePen.
- `displayOption` (DisplayOption)
- `viewDepthLimitation` (ViewDepthLimitation): Only has an effect on a multi-story wall (relativeTopStory/topOffset making it span more than one story).
- `connectionPriority` (integer): Priority of the wall in a junction with other elements (API_WallType::wallConnPriority - higher wins the cut/cover at the junction). Archicad ignores writes to this field; read-only in practice.
- `useCompositePriority` (boolean): When true, the Composite's own priority is used at junctions instead of connectionPriority.
- `junctionSequence` (integer): Tie-breaker (0-999) used when two walls meet with the same connectionPriority, or when 3+ walls meet in a junction (API_WallType::sequence). Archicad ignores writes to this field; read-only in practice.
- `linkToSettings` (LinkToSettings): newCreationMode is expected to read back as false after creation; Archicad resolves the relative story selection to an absolute floor index.
- `inheritEndSurface` (boolean): The end surface of the wall is inherited from the adjoining wall.
- `alignTexture` (boolean): Align texture mapping to the wall's edges.
- `offsetFromOutside` (number): Distance between the reference line and the outside face of the wall. Output only - not settable via ModifyWalls.
- `polyCanChange` (boolean): The polygonal wall's corners can be changed in case of L and T connections. Only meaningful for a Polygonal wall (geometryType).
- `materialsChained` (boolean): Whether the surface materials are chained.
- `logHeight` (number): Height of the log for log walls. 0 means a normal (non-log) wall.
- `hasWindow` (boolean): Whether the wall has at least one Window. Output only.
- `hasDoor` (boolean): Whether the wall has at least one Door. Output only.

### BeamDetails

object
- `begCoordinate` (Coordinate2D, required)
- `endCoordinate` (Coordinate2D, required)
- `zCoordinate` (number, required)
- `level` (number, required): base height of the beam relative to the floor level
- `offset` (number, required): beam ref.line offset from the center
- `slantAngle` (number, required): The slant angle of the beam in radians.
- `arcAngle` (number, required): The arc angle of the (horizontally) curved beam in radians.
- `verticalCurveHeight` (number, required): The height of the vertical curve of the beam.
- `beamShape` (string ("Straight", "HorizontallyCurved", "VerticallyCurved"))
- `isSlanted` (boolean)
- `isFlipped` (boolean)
- `profileAngle` (number)
- `anchorPoint` (BeamAnchorPoint)
- `cutFillPen` (OverriddenPen)
- `cutFillBackgroundPen` (OverriddenPen)
- `coverFill` (CoverFill)
- `holes` (array of BeamHole)
- `width` (number): Cross section width of the beam (all segments).
- `height` (number): Cross section height of the beam (all segments).
- `circleBased` (boolean): True for a round beam cross section, false for rectangular.
- `isWidthAndHeightLinked` (boolean): When true, Archicad keeps width and height equal - set to false via ModifyBeams/CreateBeams to give them independent values.
- `buildingMaterialId` (AttributeId): Present when the cross section uses a building material rather than a custom profile.
- `profileId` (AttributeId): Present when the cross section uses a custom extruded profile rather than a building material.
- `segments` (array of BeamSegmentSurfaces): The surfaces of each segment of the beam.

### RoofDetails

object
- `roofClass` (string ("SinglePlane", "MultiPlane"), required)
- `structureType` (RoofStructureType, required)
- `thickness` (number, required)
- `level` (number, required): Height of the pivot line (single-plane) or the pivot polygon (multi-plane) above the floor level.
- `zCoordinate` (number, required)
- `buildingMaterialId` (AttributeId)
- `compositeId` (AttributeId)
- `topMaterial` (OverriddenMaterial)
- `sideMaterial` (OverriddenMaterial)
- `bottomMaterial` (OverriddenMaterial)
- `materialsChained` (boolean): Whether the surface materials are chained.
- `displayOption` (DisplayOption)
- `viewDepthLimitation` (ViewDepthLimitation)
- `isAutoOnStoryVisibility` (boolean): When true, Archicad recomputes 'visibility' and 'fillVisibility' automatically from the roof's vertical extent.
- `visibility` (StoryVisibility): The stories the roof's contour is shown on (API_ShellBaseType::visibilityCont).
- `fillVisibility` (StoryVisibility): The stories the roof's cover fill is shown on (API_ShellBaseType::visibilityFill).
- `cutBodyType` (string ("Editable", "ContoursDown", "PivotLinesDown", "UpwardsExtrusion", "DownwardsExtrusion")): How the roof's body is extended for connections with other elements (API_ShellBaseType::cutBodyType, on the Model panel of Roof Settings).
- `cutFillPen` (OverriddenPen)
- `cutFillBackgroundPen` (OverriddenPen)
- `sectionContourPen` (integer): Pen of the roof's contour where it is cut (API_ShellBaseType::sectContPen).
- `sectionContourLineTypeId` (AttributeId): Line type of the roof's contour where it is cut (API_ShellBaseType::sectContLtype) - pairs with sectionContourPen.
- `contourPen` (integer): Pen of the roof's contour (API_ShellBaseType::pen).
- `contourLineTypeId` (AttributeId): Line type of the roof's contour (API_ShellBaseType::ltypeInd) - pairs with contourPen.
- `aboveViewLinePen` (integer): Pen used when "Overhead All" is selected from the "Floor Plan Display" popup.
- `aboveViewLineTypeId` (AttributeId): Line type used when "Overhead All" is selected from the "Floor Plan Display" popup - pairs with aboveViewLinePen.
- `floorFill` (ShellBaseFloorFill)
- `angle` (number): Single-plane: the slope in radians.
- `pivotLine` (RoofDetailsPivotLine): For single-plane roofs.
- `eavesOverhang` (number): Multi-plane: the eaves overhang beyond the pivot polygon.
- `levels` (array of RoofDetailsLevel): Multi-plane: the roof levels, each with its height above the previous and its slope in radians.
- `pivotPolygonOutline` (array of Coordinate2D): Multi-plane: the pivot polygon the planes rise from. Arcs are not carried; a curved pivot edge comes back as its end points.
- `polygonOutline` (array of Coordinate2D, required): The roof's polygon: the plane roof's outline, the multi-plane roof's contour.
- `polygonArcs` (array of PolyArc)
- `holes` (Holes2D)
- `edgeSideMaterials` (array of OverriddenMaterial): The custom side surface of each edge of the roof's polygon: the edges of polygonOutline first, then those of each hole in order, the item i of a polygon belonging to its edge from vertex i to vertex i + 1.
- `edgeTrims` (array of RoofEdgeTrim): Single-plane roofs only: the cut of each edge of the roof's polygon, in the order of edgeSideMaterials. ModifyRoofs takes the same list.
- `pivotEdges` (array of object): Multi-plane roofs only: the roof planes of each edge of the pivot polygon. Item i belongs to the edge from vertex i to vertex i + 1 of pivotPolygonOutline; for a pivot polygon with holes, the edges of each hole follow, contour by contour.
  - `levels` (array of object, required): The roof plane of the edge on each level, from the pivot polygon upwards.
